claims.text: Rapid solidification followed by two-step annealing will refine the grain structure of MnNiSi-based alloys.
The resulting grain refinement will improve mechanical performance.
The proposed processing will retain a strong magnetocaloric effect.
Conventional slow cooling of the MnNiSi-based alloy produces a relatively coarse grain structure.
A lower-temperature anneal will provide structural relaxation.
A subsequent higher-temperature anneal will produce recrystallization.
An inert processing atmosphere will prevent oxidation.
Appropriate control of cooling rate, annealing temperature, and annealing time can avoid detrimental secondary phases.
The proposed process will produce a refined grain structure with increased grain-boundary density.
Increased grain-boundary density will strengthen the alloy through the Hall-Petch effect.
The phase transformation responsible for the magnetocaloric effect will remain largely unaltered if processing causes no significant compositional or phase changes.
The treated alloy will have greater ductility than the conventionally processed baseline.
The treated alloy will have greater yield strength than the conventionally processed baseline.
The treated alloy's isothermal entropy change near the transition will be similar to or only marginally lower than that of the conventionally processed material.
Conventionally slow-cooled MnNiSi-based material has moderate mechanical performance and a large magnetocaloric effect.
Excessive grain refinement may induce embrittlement or precipitate formation.
Poorly optimized rapid-solidification or annealing parameters may alter the phase transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
